data_fields.name: crit_chance_pct
data_fields.donor_constant: h.crit_chance (filled by the power code, value not read), modified by MULTIPLY / ADD / ABSOLUTE modes

data_fields.name: crit_impaired_bonus
data_fields.donor_constant: trait_crits_impaired added when the defender is stunned or speed below 100 (per power, value not read)

data_fields.name: crit_max_pct
data_fields.donor_constant: 200 (clamped up to the min when the settings file is read)

data_fields.name: crit_shake_ticks
data_fields.donor_constant: max_frames_per_sec / 2 (half a second of logic frames)

data_fields.name: shake_strength
data_fields.donor_constant: 8 (offsets of -8 to +7 units, scaled by 1/128 tile)

best_idea: A killing blow that lands as a crit enters a separate finisher death state, decided in the same damage step, and only when the foe has a finisher clip; the sound, the clip and the corpse are cosmetic and follow that state.
decision_why: Take the crit-kill state split and the rule that heroes never take the finisher; reject the client-side crit roll and client-side death, because Frankendom's server must decide crit and kill and the client only plays the finisher.
acceptance: When the server's damage result reports a crit kill on a foe whose catalogue has a finisher clip, the foe plays that clip with one random sound from its list; its death AI power fires at the clip's second-last frame; it leaves a corpse that fades after the zone's corpse time. A normal kill plays the plain death and a hero death never plays the finisher; a server test asserts the crit flag and the kill come from the same damage result.
